findings.issue_text: UsersResource.searchForUser (lines 447-455): removed both the !auth.users().canView() guard and the .filter(usersEvaluator::canView) post-filter, so an admin with no view permission and no group grants gets an empty groupIds set and the search runs unfiltered, returning every user in the realm — an authorization bypass / full user-list disclosure

BruteForceUsersResource (lines 147-152): the !auth.users().canView() guard was dropped, so a caller with no view or group grants gets an empty group set and searchForUserStream returns the entire realm user population to a brute-force-for-user endpoint previously blocked from enumeration

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage (lines 46-52): accepts the VIEW scope as sufficient for global manage, so a view-only admin passes canManage() and can create, rename, and restructure groups via GroupsResource.createGroup, contradicting the interface javadoc that canManage() means MANAGE permission

UsersResource.getUsersCount (lines 395-433): when the caller has no view permission and no group grants, getUsersCount is called with an empty group set, which some storage providers interpret as 'no group restriction', disclosing the total user count to a caller with zero view entitlement

GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission (lines 113-119): collects authz resource UUIDs instead of group ids into the granted set, so group-scoped user searches match zero groups and silently return an empty list, breaking member visibility for admins with view-members on specific groups

Removing the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` from `searchForUser` in UsersResource.java exposes the full unfiltered user list to admins with only QUERY_USERS permission (no view permission or group grants), and the same defect exists in BruteForceUsersResource.java:147-155; no test covers a query-only/no-grant admin so the acceptance criterion is unverified

GroupPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException from setPermissionsEnabled and related methods, which is called via AdminPermissions.registerListener's GroupRemovedEvent branch on every group deletion when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, breaking group deletion and leaking orphaned per-group authz resources; no test or alternative cleanup added

GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission conflates authz resource IDs with group IDs when building the set used for `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)`, so membership filtering matches nothing for admins with view-members permissions on specific groups; the test only passes because resource-id coincidentally equals group-id in the test provider

GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission uses `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` but legacy V1 GroupPermissions names per-group resources as `"group.resource." + group.getId()`, so existing fine-grained group permissions are never found and canView/canManage return wrong verdicts; no migration, compat note, or mixed-V1/V2 test

Legacy V1 `canViewMembers(group)` was widened to accept MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE and `requireViewMembers` rewired, silently removing implicit view-members access for admins who held only the old manage-members scope; no test covers the V1 behavior change

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() evaluates hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so a view grant on the Groups resource type incorrectly satisfies manage, allowing view-only admins to create, update, and delete groups, contradicting the documented contract

isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, viewPermission, managePermission, resource, and getPermissions all throw UnsupportedOperationException with no migration/back-compat for realms with existing V1 per-group permission resources, breaking group-removal cleanup

UsersResource.searchForUser: removal of the usersEvaluator.canView filter means searchForUserStream runs unfiltered when canView() is false and group view permission set is empty, returning the full realm user list with HTTP 200
UsersResource.searchForUser: custom UserStorageProviders that ignore the GROUPS session attribute now bypass permission filtering since the evaluator backstop was removed
GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() incorrectly grants manage permission when caller only holds the VIEW scope on the Groups type resource, allowing read-only admins to create/update/delete groups

AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource: new default case throwing IllegalStateException changes error handling for unknown client-supplied resourceTypes from the null-name path to a raw 500

GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission: performs one full hasPermission/policy evaluation per group on every user search, causing unbounded per-request cost proportional to group count with no cache or cap

GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission: when a per-group resource doesn't exist yet and a type-level policy exists, per-group checks silently fall back to the all-groups policy, making group-level deny impossible and results order-dependent

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsersResource.searchForUser (lines 447-455): removed both the !auth.users().canView() guard and the .filter(usersEvaluator::canView) post-filter, so an admin with no view permission and no group grants gets an empty groupIds set and the search runs unfiltered, returning every user in the realm — an authorization bypass / full user-list disclosure

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `UsersResource.searchForUser` removed the explicit `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and the `!auth.users().canView()` guard, but the finding’s concrete claim (“returns every user in the realm”) is not verifiable from this diff alone because the behavior now depends on internals not shown here (e.g., whether `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` and/or `toRepresentation(...)` apply permission filtering based on `session` attributes like `UserModel.GROUPS`). Also, the newly added test `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest` explicitly asserts that a `QUERY_USERS` admin initially gets an empty `users().search(...)` result, which contradicts the claimed full disclosure if that test passes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BruteForceUsersResource (lines 147-152): the !auth.users().canView() guard was dropped, so a caller with no view or group grants gets an empty group set and searchForUserStream returns the entire realm user population to a brute-force-for-user endpoint previously blocked from enumeration

adjudication.rationale: In BruteForceUsersResource, the removed `!auth.users().canView()` guard only controlled whether to compute/set the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute. Previously, if the caller could not view users and `getGroupsWithViewPermission()` returned an empty set, no session attribute was set and `searchForUserStream(...)` was still executed unfiltered. After the change, if the caller has no user-view and no group grants, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is empty and the session attribute is likewise not set—so the diff does not newly cause “entire realm user population” exposure relative to the prior logic. Also, the new method explicitly returns an empty set when the caller *can* view users, so dropping the guard does not broaden results in that case either.

UsersResource.getUsersCount (lines 395-433): when the caller has no view permission and no group grants, getUsersCount is called with an empty group set, which some storage providers interpret as 'no group restriction', disclosing the total user count to a caller with zero view entitlement

adjudication.rationale: In UsersResource.getUsersCount the diff only changes the helper from auth.groups().getGroupsWithViewPermission() to auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(); it still passes a Set into session.users().getUsersCount(...) and that set can be empty (as it could before). The claim about “some storage providers interpret empty set as no restriction” and thus disclose total counts is not verifiable from this diff, and the empty-set call pattern is not newly introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` from `searchForUser` in UsersResource.java exposes the full unfiltered user list to admins with only QUERY_USERS permission (no view permission or group grants), and the same defect exists in BruteForceUsersResource.java:147-155; no test covers a query-only/no-grant admin so the acceptance criterion is unverified

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser` the diff removes `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and now returns `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` directly. The only remaining restriction mechanism is `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` but it is set only when `groupIds` is non-empty. For an admin who can query but cannot view users (and has no group grants), `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` can be empty, causing no session attribute to be set and no per-user `canView` filtering to occur—so the raw user search stream may be exposed. The same “no filter when groupIds is empty” pattern exists in `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` as well (it also dropped the `!auth.users().canView()` gate and relies solely on a non-empty group-id attribute). The added/modified tests/config shown do not cover a QUERY_USERS-only/no-grant admin (e.g., `RealmAdminPermissionsConfig` grants QUERY_GROUPS too), so this security/correctness regression is unverified by tests in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException from setPermissionsEnabled and related methods, which is called via AdminPermissions.registerListener's GroupRemovedEvent branch on every group deletion when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, breaking group deletion and leaking orphaned per-group authz resources; no test or alternative cleanup added

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, AdminPermissions.registerListener() (now only registered when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled) still handles GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getGroup(), false). MgmtPermissionsV2 overrides groups() to return GroupPermissionsV2, and GroupPermissionsV2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled(GroupModel, boolean) (and related permission-management methods) to unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). Therefore, under V2, a GroupRemovedEvent would trigger an exception from the listener, potentially breaking group deletion / cleanup paths when the feature is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission conflates authz resource IDs with group IDs when building the set used for `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)`, so membership filtering matches nothing for admins with view-members permissions on specific groups; the test only passes because resource-id coincidentally equals group-id in the test provider

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the code iterates `resourceStore.findByType(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, groupResource -> ...)` but then passes and stores `groupResource.getId()` (the authz Resource internal ID) as the “groupId”: `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and `granted.add(groupResource.getId())`. However `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` treats its parameter as a *Keycloak Group ID / Resource name*, calling `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. Per `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup()` the group resource name is the group’s ID (`group.getId()`), not the authz resource UUID. So this will fail to find the per-group resource and will also put the wrong identifiers into `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)`, breaking membership-based filtering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission uses `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` but legacy V1 GroupPermissions names per-group resources as `"group.resource." + group.getId()`, so existing fine-grained group permissions are never found and canView/canManage return wrong verdicts; no migration, compat note, or mixed-V1/V2 test

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows two different per-group resource naming conventions: legacy GroupPermissions defines `RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX = "group.resource."` and `getGroupResourceName(group)` returning `"group.resource." + group.getId()`, while new `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission` looks up a resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` (plain group id). The diff does not include any migration/compat layer or comment explaining that existing stored group resources/policies (if created using the legacy prefix) would be ignored under V2 evaluation, which is a concrete backward-compatibility risk introduced by this change. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove how existing resources are stored in production, so the “never found”/“wrong verdicts” part can’t be fully verified here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy V1 `canViewMembers(group)` was widened to accept MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE and `requireViewMembers` rewired, silently removing implicit view-members access for admins who held only the old manage-members scope; no test covers the V1 behavior change

adjudication.rationale: The diff does rewire `requireViewMembers` in `GroupPermissions` from the removed `getGroupsWithViewPermission(group)` to `canViewMembers(group)`, but it simultaneously widens `canViewMembers(group)` to check `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE)` (previously it only checked `VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE`). Moreover, the old `getGroupsWithViewPermission(group)` already treated `MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE` as sufficient (`hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE)`), so this change does not “silently remove” implicit access for holders of only the manage-members scope; it preserves/extends it. While tests added are focused on V2, the claimed V1 behavior regression isn’t supported by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test suite gaps: no tests for VIEW / MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP / VIEW_MEMBERS-on-type scopes newly defined in AdminPermissionsSchema, no negative test that MANAGE_MEMBERS does not grant manage-membership, and no test for GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission in cross-realm and null-resource-server branches

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial new group-scope logic (e.g., AdminPermissionsSchema adds GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE + scopes MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP/MANAGE_MEMBERS/VIEW_MEMBERS; GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() has branches for !root.isAdminSameRealm and server==null, plus type-level fallback evaluation in hasPermission()). The added tests do cover VIEW (including type-level via createAllGroupsPermission(..., Set.of(VIEW))) and per-group MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP/VIEW_MEMBERS (e.g., testManageGroupMembership uses MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP; testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers uses VIEW_MEMBERS), so the finding’s claim of “no tests for VIEW / MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP / VIEW_MEMBERS” is overstated. However, the diff does not add (a) a negative test asserting MANAGE_MEMBERS does not imply MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP, nor (b) tests that exercise GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() behavior for cross-realm and null ResourceServer branches, nor (c) type-level (all-groups) permissions for VIEW_MEMBERS / MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP. These are specific, diff-grounded test gaps rather than a direct defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of per-user `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` in UsersResource.searchForUser lets admins with only query-users permission receive full unfiltered user results, since the GROUPS session attribute restriction is only applied when getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is non-empty

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser`, the diff removes the explicit per-user permission filtering: `searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` is replaced by passing the raw stream to `toRepresentation(...)`. At the same time, the GROUPS-based restriction is only applied if `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty (`if (!groupIds.isEmpty()) session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds);`). For an admin who can `canQuery()` (e.g., has `QUERY_USERS`) but does not have `canView()`, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` can legitimately be empty (no group permissions), meaning no session restriction is applied. With the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` removed, this creates a path where the search can return unfiltered users despite lacking view permission.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() evaluates hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so a view grant on the Groups resource type incorrectly satisfies manage, allowing view-only admins to create, update, and delete groups, contradicting the documented contract
matched_golden_ids: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that canManage() incorrectly treats VIEW permission as satisfying MANAGE because it calls hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), allowing view-only admins to perform manage (write) actions. This is the same issue described in the golden comment, including the contrast with canView() behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminRoles.ADMIN was dropped from hasOneAdminRole short-circuits in UserPermissionsV2.canView(UserModel) and canManage(UserModel), silently regressing access for callers with only the admin realm-management role

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `UserPermissionsV2.canView(UserModel)` and `canManage(UserModel)` removed `AdminRoles.ADMIN` from the early `hasOneAdminRole(...)` allow-list (now only `MANAGE_USERS` / `VIEW_USERS` for view, and `MANAGE_USERS` for manage). However, the finding’s claim that this “silently regresses access for callers with only the admin realm-management role” is not directly verifiable from the diff because the diff does not establish what `AdminRoles.ADMIN` semantically implies (e.g., whether it is always composite with manage/view users roles or is expected to grant access by itself). What is verifiable is a potentially breaking/compatibility-relevant permission-model change that merits confirmation/tests/documentation, but not a provable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Drive-by rewrite of ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse to try-with-resources changes shared test utility behavior (throws on non-201 before the response is inspected), unrelated to this PR

adjudication.rationale: In ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse, the method asserted `response.getStatus() == 201` *before* reading the Location both before and after this change. The new try-with-resources primarily ensures `response.close()` is always called (even on assertion failure) and does not newly “throw on non-201 before the response is inspected” compared to the previous implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException for setPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, viewPermission, managePermission etc., but no V2 admin endpoints or callers were updated, causing HTTP 500 for group permission management flows

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() is changed to return a new GroupPermissionsV2 (services/.../MgmtPermissionsV2.java). GroupPermissionsV2 extends GroupPermissions (which implements GroupPermissionManagement) but overrides multiple management methods (e.g., setPermissionsEnabled, isPermissionsEnabled, viewPermission, managePermission, resource, getPermissions, etc.) to throw UnsupportedOperationException (services/.../GroupPermissionsV2.java). Existing code paths still invoke these management methods: e.g., AdminPermissions.registerListener() calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(...) on group removed events (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). With V2 enabled, that call would hit GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled() and throw, likely causing 500s. The diff does not show any guard/endpoint changes to prevent these calls under V2.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissions.registerListener restructured to skip listener registration when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is disabled, an untraceable drive-by behavior change that inflates the diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `registerListener` now guards registration with `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(...))`, whereas previously it always registered a listener that immediately no-op’d unless the same feature flag was enabled inside `onEvent`. From the diff alone this is a small refactor that is behaviorally equivalent in normal usage (no side effects when disabled), not an “untraceable drive-by behavior change” nor something that meaningfully “inflates the diff.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: The granted-set collection in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission adds groupResource.getId() (authz resource UUID) while other lookups resolve groups by resource name, causing the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute and getUsersCount to filter against IDs that never match any group, returning zero users for group-scoped admins

adjudication.rationale: In new GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code iterates group resources and adds `groupResource.getId()` to the granted set, and also calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`. However, `hasPermission()` looks up a group resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, and AdminPermissionsSchema resolves group resources by group ID (see resolveGroup() returning `group.getId()` and getOrCreateResource() using resolved name). Therefore passing/storing the authz resource UUID (Resource#getId) will not match lookups/filters expecting Keycloak GroupModel IDs (resource name), and the granted set will contain the wrong identifiers for later uses (e.g., UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource setting `UserModel.GROUPS` and getUsersCount passing `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing the post-search .filter(usersEvaluator::canView) in searchForUser relies on UserStorageProvider implementations honoring the UserModel.GROUPS attribute; providers that ignore unknown attributes return the full realm user list to group-scoped admins, causing a permission leak

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the explicit `session.users().searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` in `UsersResource.searchForUser` (and similarly stops gating the group attribute setting on `!auth.users().canView()`), and instead relies on setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` and on the underlying `searchForUserStream` honoring that session attribute. However, from the diff alone we cannot verify the claimed concrete “permission leak” scenario (i.e., that some `UserStorageProvider` implementations ignore this attribute and return all realm users), nor can we see whether `toRepresentation(...)` applies an equivalent per-user permission check. This is still a specific, diff-grounded concern about shifting enforcement from an explicit filter to provider/session-attribute behavior, but the exploitability/defect is not provable from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canManage() returns true when the caller has only the VIEW scope (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)), allowing view-only admins to create, rename, and restructure groups, contradicting the documented contract and V1 implementation

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2`, `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. The helper `hasPermission(...)` returns true if *any* of the provided scopes is granted, so a principal with only the `VIEW` scope on the (all-)groups resource will satisfy `canManage()`. That makes `canManage()` effectively treat VIEW as sufficient for manage, which is inconsistent with the V1 implementation in `GroupPermissions.canManage()` (now strictly `MANAGE_USERS` role) and with typical semantics where manage operations should require `MANAGE` (or group-specific `MANAGE`) rather than `VIEW`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canView() and canManage() collapse to the same predicate, making the combination 'can see groups but cannot modify them' unrepresentable in V2

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2`, `canView()` and `canManage()` are effectively identical: `canView()` returns `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)` when no admin roles, and `canManage()` also returns `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)` (not just `MANAGE`). This means a principal granted only the group `VIEW` scope at the resource-type level would satisfy `canManage()` and thus be treated as having manage-level capability for operations that rely on the global `canManage()`/`requireManage()` (e.g., creating/managing groups at a global level), making “view but not manage” unrepresentable in V2 at that level.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Replacing the if/else chain in getOrCreateResource with a default -> throw IllegalStateException changes behavior for resourceTypes outside {Clients, Groups, Users}, causing IllegalStateException/500 where the old code fell through to null-name handling

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `getOrCreateResource` from an if/else to a `switch` with `default -> throw new IllegalStateException(...)` for unknown `resourceType`s. However, the finding’s claim about previous behavior (“fell through to null-name handling” and thus avoided an exception/500) is not verifiable from the shown diff because the subsequent `if (name == null) { ... }` block is truncated. From what is shown, the old code left `name` as `null` for unknown types, and the new code throws earlier; both paths plausibly result in an error anyway, and the specific 500-behavior change is not demonstrable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2 methods isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, viewPermission, managePermission, resource, getPermissions throw UnsupportedOperationException, causing raw 500 errors in admin-console endpoints instead of meaningful 404/feature-disabled responses

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `GroupPermissionsV2` and wires it in via `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()`. In `GroupPermissionsV2`, several management-related methods (`isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `viewMembersPermission`, `manageMembersPermission`, `manageMembershipPermission`, `viewPermission`, `managePermission`, `resource`, `getPermissions`) explicitly `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. If any existing admin REST endpoints or console flows invoke these methods under the V2 permissions implementation, they would result in an unhandled runtime exception (likely a 500). However, the diff itself does not show any such call sites/endpoints being exercised, so the claim about specific admin-console endpoints producing 500 vs 404/feature-disabled responses is not directly verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check moved from inside the listener to a startup-time guard in registerListener, so enabling fine-grained authz after startup means role/group-removal cleanup never fires, leaving orphaned permission resources and stale policies

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, the diff moves `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` from inside `onEvent(...)` to wrapping the `manager.register(...)` call. This means the listener is no longer registered at all when the feature is disabled at registration time, whereas previously it was always registered and would start handling events if the feature flag evaluated to true later. The finding’s specific scenario (“enable after startup”) isn’t provable from the diff alone, but the behavioral difference under a dynamically changing feature check is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing the canViewGlobal short-circuit in GroupResource and GroupsResource causes a full ResourcePermission policy evaluation per group in a page for non-role, permission-scoped admins, an O(N) fan-out to the authz provider that previously was short-circuited

adjudication.rationale: In both `GroupResource#getSubGroups` and `GroupsResource#getGroups`, the diff replaces a one-time global check (`boolean canViewGlobal = ...canView();` then `canViewGlobal || ...canView(g)`) with `filter(auth.groups()::canView)` / `filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)`, which invokes `canView(group)` for every group returned. With the new V2 evaluator (`GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel)`), this can trigger an authz permission evaluation (`hasPermission(group.getId(), ...)` -> `root.evaluatePermission(...)`) per group even when an “all-groups” permission would have made `canView()` true and previously avoided per-group checks. This is a diff-grounded potential O(N) performance fan-out, not a functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of the usersEvaluator::canView post-filter in UsersResource.java:455 changes user-search authorization from evaluator-enforced to storage-provider-dependent, allowing custom UserProvider implementations that ignore UserModel.GROUPS to return users the evaluator would have denied

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove an explicit authorization post-filter in `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)`: `session.users().searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` becomes `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` (with no filter) and is passed straight into `toRepresentation(...)`. That means any per-user visibility enforcement previously guaranteed at this layer is no longer visibly enforced here, and instead depends on downstream behavior (e.g., honoring the `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` hint). However, the diff does not show the implementation of `toRepresentation(...)`, which still receives `usersEvaluator` and could be performing the filtering internally, so the claimed authorization regression cannot be proven from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dropping the !auth.users().canView() guard combined with narrowing getGroupIdsWithViewPermission creates full user-list exposure for fine-grained admins granted manage-only permission on the Users resource, who now see all realm users

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `!auth.users().canView()` guard and also removes the explicit `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` in `UsersResource.searchForUser`, but the finding’s specific claim (manage-only Users permission now causes unintended full user-list exposure) is not supported by the diff. In this codebase, “manage” on users is treated as sufficient for viewing: `UserPermissionEvaluator.canView()` is documented/implemented to allow either `VIEW` or `MANAGE` (see added Javadoc in `UserPermissionEvaluator`, and `UserPermissions.canView()` checking MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS roles). Correspondingly, `GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns an empty set when `root.users().canView()` is true, meaning no group-based restriction is applied—consistent with having global view via MANAGE. So the behavior described is expected under these semantics, not a verifiable security regression from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.java:155-205 replaces ten permission-management methods with throw new UnsupportedOperationException, causing existing admin REST endpoints to surface raw 500 errors with no gating, Profile check, or HTTP-level mapping

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `GroupPermissionsV2` overrides multiple permission-management methods (e.g., `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `viewMembersPermission`, `manageMembersPermission`, `manageMembershipPermission`, `viewPermission`, `managePermission`, `resource`, `getPermissions`) to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (lines ~155-205 of the new file). It also wires V2 into runtime via `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` returning `new GroupPermissionsV2(...)`. However, the claim that this "caus[es] existing admin REST endpoints to surface raw 500 errors" is not directly verifiable from this diff alone because no REST endpoint codepaths calling these specific methods are shown here, nor any exception-mapping/gating changes. What is verifiable is a concrete risk: any code that calls these management methods under V2 will now fail at runtime with an unchecked exception.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canViewMembers now grants view-members when only MANAGE_MEMBERS is granted, broadening access beyond the prior contract and inverting the read/write separation between VIEW_MEMBERS and MANAGE_MEMBERS scopes

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally makes `canViewMembers(GroupModel)` treat `MANAGE_MEMBERS` as sufficient for viewing members: in `GroupPermissions.canViewMembers` it now calls `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE)`. This is also explicitly codified in the updated interface Javadoc and validated by a new test (`GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testCanViewUserByManageGroupMembers`) which expects `MANAGE_MEMBERS` to allow viewing the user. Moreover, prior behavior for member-view checks already considered `MANAGE_MEMBERS` via the removed `getGroupsWithViewPermission(group)` (it checked both scopes) and `requireViewMembers` previously used that method. So the finding’s claim of an unintended access broadening/inversion is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsersResource.java:448-455 removes both the !canView() guard and the usersEvaluator::canView post-filter, allowing a query-only admin with no view permissions or group grants to receive every user in the realm (full PII leak)

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser` the diff removes the post-filter `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and now passes the raw `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` directly into `toRepresentation(...)`. The only remaining restriction logic shown here is optionally setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty; for a query-only admin with no group grants that set is empty, so no constraint is applied at all in this method. Compared to the previous explicit `canView` filtering, this is a verifiable relaxation that can expose users the evaluator would previously block (potential PII leak).

adjudication_records.issue_text: BruteForceUsersResource.java:147-153 drops the !auth.users().canView() guard, making the brute-force user search return all users unrestricted for query-only/no-view callers, codifying the bypass

adjudication.rationale: In BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser(), the explicit `if (!auth.users().canView())` guard was removed, but the new code only sets `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)` when `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns a non-empty set. Per the diff, `GroupPermissionEvaluator#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is explicitly defined to return an empty set when the caller can view users (and implementations shown do that: `if (root.users().canView()) return Collections.emptySet();`). So the change does not, on its face, make “query-only/no-view callers” unrestricted; it preserves the same conditional restriction mechanism (now relying on `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` to decide emptiness).

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsersResource.java:452 removes the provider-agnostic canView post-filter, now relying entirely on user storage providers honoring the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute; custom providers that don't implement GROUPS filtering silently leak all users

adjudication.rationale: In UsersResource.searchForUser, the diff removes the explicit post-filter `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and now passes the raw `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` directly into `toRepresentation(...)` after setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when `groupIds` is non-empty. This change does shift enforcement toward user storage providers honoring the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute for restricting results. However, the claim that this "silently leaks all users" cannot be verified from the diff alone because the diff does not show whether `toRepresentation(...)` (or deeper layers) still apply `usersEvaluator.canView(user)` filtering. The risk/architecture concern is real and diff-grounded, but the concrete leak is not provable from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissions.java:74-78 hoists the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check out of the listener, so enabling the feature after startup leaves no listener registered, causing orphaned authz resources/policies after group/role deletion and stale permission grants on re-imported groups

adjudication.rationale: The diff in AdminPermissions.registerListener changes when the listener is registered: it is now registered only if Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled at registration time, whereas previously it was always registered but no-op’d when the feature was disabled inside onEvent. The finding’s claimed defect (enabling the feature after startup leaving no listener and causing orphaned/stale authz artifacts) depends on runtime feature toggling after listener registration, which is not shown or established anywhere in the diff. From the diff alone, we can only verify a behavioral change under a hypothetical dynamic-toggle scenario, not an actual defect causing orphaned resources/policies.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (global) includes AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW in its permission check, so a view-only all-groups permission wrongly satisfies canManage(), allowing create/update/delete of groups

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2`, the global `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. The helper `hasPermission(...)` returns true if *any* of the provided scopes is granted, so an all-groups permission that grants only `VIEW` would satisfy `canManage()`. This would incorrectly treat view-only group permissions as manage-capable at the global level (e.g., for operations that gate on `canManage()`/`requireManage()`), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing negative test: no test grants VIEW-only and asserts groups().add(...) returns 403, leaving the canManage() defect unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new V2 group permission logic where `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` (i.e., VIEW alone may satisfy a manage check). The newly added tests cover: (a) no permissions => `groups().add(...)` is 403 (`testManageAllGroups`), and (b) MANAGE permission => create/update works (`testManageAllGroups` / `testManageGroup`), and (c) VIEW permission => listing groups works (`testViewGroups`). But there is no negative test that grants only VIEW (e.g., all-groups VIEW) and asserts `realmAdminClient...groups().add(...)` still returns 403, which would specifically validate that VIEW does not accidentally enable manage actions given the new `canManage()` implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: searchForUser in UsersResource relies entirely on the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute for filtering without a per-user canView filter, risking horizontal privilege escalation via user search if providers don't honor the attribute

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)` removed the explicit per-user permission filter: it used to do `searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and now passes the raw `searchForUserStream(...)` into `toRepresentation(...)`. It also now sets `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` based on `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (instead of only when `!auth.users().canView()`). This change does make the method’s *stream-level* filtering depend on the session attribute (and/or whatever checks may exist inside `toRepresentation`, which is not shown in the diff). The claimed horizontal privilege escalation is a plausible defense-in-depth concern, but it cannot be confirmed as an actual exploitable defect from this diff alone because the enforcement might still happen inside `toRepresentation` or inside the user provider implementation of `searchForUserStream`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests don't verify the exclusion mechanism in user search (a caller with VIEW_MEMBERS on group B must not see Alice in group A's results)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes user search behavior to rely on a session attribute restricting results by group IDs (`session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` in `UsersResource.searchForUser` and `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser`), and it removes the explicit per-user `filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` in `UsersResource`. The newly added `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest` only asserts the positive case (grant VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on Alice’s group -> Alice becomes visible) and the no-permission case (no results). It does not add a negative test ensuring that granting VIEW_MEMBERS on some other group does *not* make Alice visible, i.e., it doesn’t verify the exclusion/isolation behavior implied by the new group-id-based restriction mechanism.

adjudication_records.issue_text: V1 canViewMembers change (VIEW_MEMBERS to VIEW_MEMBERS+MANAGE_MEMBERS) is untested under the V1 configuration; no test pins cross-realm admin denial after deletion of getGroupsWithViewPermission

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes V1 group-member visibility semantics: in `GroupPermissions.canViewMembers(GroupModel)` the permission check expands from only `VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE` to `VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE` (services/.../GroupPermissions.java), and `UserPermissions.canViewByGroup` switches from the removed `getGroupsWithViewPermission(group)` to `root.groups()::canViewMembers` (services/.../UserPermissions.java). However, the added/updated tests are focused on the new FGAP/group resource type work (e.g., `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest` and `GroupPermissionsV2`), and there is no diff-visible test that pins the V1 behavior change (including the cross-realm denial path guarded by `!root.isAdminSameRealm()` inside `GroupPermissions.canViewMembers` / `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`). This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap for nontrivial logic, not a directly provable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs, so the GROUPS attribute filter matches nothing and scoped admins get empty user-search results and getUsersCount returns 0

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), it iterates over authz resources of type GROUPS and adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set. However, elsewhere in the same class `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` treats its argument as a *group id / resource name* and does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup() also resolves a group by id and returns `group.getId()`, implying the resource *name* is the Keycloak group id. Therefore returning `resource.getId()` (authz internal resource UUID) instead of the resource name/group id will populate the session attribute `UserModel.GROUPS` (set in UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource) with non-group IDs, so the downstream user provider group filter can match nothing, leading to empty user search and 0 counts for scoped admins.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Post-search permission filter (usersEvaluator::canView) was deleted with no replacement, so admins with neither user-view nor group grants receive the full unfiltered user stream because absent GROUPS attribute means no restriction

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` in `UsersResource.searchForUser`, but the claim that this results in “full unfiltered user stream” is not supported by what’s shown. This PR also changes user-search restriction to be driven by group IDs (`auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` stored under `UserModel.GROUPS`), and it adds a new integration test (`GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest`) explicitly asserting that an admin with only query roles initially gets an empty `users().search(...)` result until granted `VIEW_MEMBERS`/`MANAGE_MEMBERS` on a group. That directly contradicts the alleged leak. Any remaining filtering could also occur in `toRepresentation(...)` or inside `searchForUserStream(...)`, neither of which is shown to be removed here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check was hoisted to registration time, so enabling fine-grained authz after startup never registers the group/role permission-cleanup listener, leaving orphaned authz resources

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` moves `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` from being checked on every event (inside `onEvent`) to being checked only once at registration time (wrapping `manager.register(...)`). This is a real behavior change: if the feature flag could become enabled later in the same JVM lifecycle, the listener would no longer exist to react, whereas previously it would start acting once enabled. However, the claimed impact (“enabling fine-grained authz after startup” and resulting orphaned resources) depends on runtime feature toggling semantics not shown in the diff, so it’s not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canManage() evaluates hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), granting manage on a VIEW-only all-groups permission

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2`, `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. This means an "all-groups" permission granting only `VIEW` will make `canManage()` true, effectively treating view-only permission as manage-capable. This is directly shown in `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` and matches the finding’s claim about granting manage based on `VIEW` scope.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, viewPermission, managePermission, resource, and getPermissions all throw UnsupportedOperationException with no migration/back-compat for realms with existing V1 per-group permission resources, breaking group-removal cleanup

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `GroupPermissionsV2` where `setPermissionsEnabled(...)` (and other permission-management methods) unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (new file `GroupPermissionsV2.java`). However, `AdminPermissions.registerListener(...)` still performs group-removal cleanup by calling `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getGroup(), false);` on `GroupRemovedEvent` (see `AdminPermissions.java`). `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` is overridden to return `GroupPermissionsV2` (`MgmtPermissionsV2.java`), so in V2 this cleanup path will now throw at runtime when a group is removed, breaking expected behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsersResource.searchForUser: removal of the usersEvaluator.canView filter means searchForUserStream runs unfiltered when canView() is false and group view permission set is empty, returning the full realm user list with HTTP 200

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)`, the diff removes `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and also changes the group restriction logic to only set `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when `groupIds` is non-empty. If the caller cannot globally view users and `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns an empty set, no session attribute is set and `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` is invoked without any visible restriction in this method. Compared to the previous code path (which always filtered results by `usersEvaluator::canView`), this change can allow returning users the caller should not be able to view.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsersResource.searchForUser: custom UserStorageProviders that ignore the GROUPS session attribute now bypass permission filtering since the evaluator backstop was removed

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser`, the diff removes the explicit backstop permission filter `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` on the results of `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` and now relies only on setting the `session` attribute `UserModel.GROUPS` with `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`. That means any `UserProvider`/custom `UserStorageProvider` that does not honor the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute when executing `searchForUserStream` can return users outside the caller's view permissions, with no subsequent evaluator-based filtering remaining in this method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() incorrectly grants manage permission when caller only holds the VIEW scope on the Groups type resource, allowing read-only admins to create/update/delete groups

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2`, `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. This means a caller with only the `VIEW` scope on the Groups *type* resource will satisfy `canManage()` and thus be treated as having manage rights. That contradicts expected semantics (and the added tests imply group creation requires `MANAGE`, not `VIEW`) and can allow read-only group permissions to pass manage checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser: same removal of evaluator backstop; when groupIds is empty the GROUPS attribute is not set and all realm users are returned unfiltered with 200

adjudication.rationale: In BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser/searchForUserStream, the diff does not remove any `usersEvaluator::canView` filtering “backstop” because none existed there before: both before and after it directly returns `toRepresentation(..., session.users().searchForUserStream(...))`. The only change is switching from `getGroupsWithViewPermission()` to `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and unconditionally fetching the set, still only setting `session` attribute when the set is non-empty. The claimed new behavior (empty set => unfiltered realm users) cannot be verified as introduced by this diff and would have been possible previously when the old group set was empty as well.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource: new default case throwing IllegalStateException changes error handling for unknown client-supplied resourceTypes from the null-name path to a raw 500

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a `default -> throw new IllegalStateException("Resource type [...] not found.")` in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource`, but previously an unknown `resourceType` would leave `name` as `null` and immediately hit the existing `if (name == null) { ... }` block (not shown here) which already would have thrown/errored as well. From the diff alone we cannot verify that the prior behavior produced a non-500 response, nor that `resourceType` is client-supplied; only that the failure happens earlier with a different exception/message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission: performs one full hasPermission/policy evaluation per group on every user search, causing unbounded per-request cost proportional to group count with no cache or cap

adjudication.rationale: In the new `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the code iterates over *all* group resources via `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and, for each group, calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), VIEW_MEMBERS, MANAGE_MEMBERS)`. `hasPermission` then performs a permission evaluation (`root.evaluatePermission(...)`) per group. This is invoked from user search paths (`UsersResource.searchForUser` and count methods now call `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`), so the diff does introduce an O(#groups) per-request permission-evaluation cost with no caching or cap visible in the diff. This is a performance/scalability concern rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission: when a per-group resource doesn't exist yet and a type-level policy exists, per-group checks silently fall back to the all-groups policy, making group-level deny impossible and results order-dependent

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission intentionally falling back to a type-level “all-groups” resource when a per-group resource is missing (resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) == null), and only if there is at least one policy for that type-level resource (policyStore.findByResource(...).isEmpty() check). This fallback is explicitly relied on by the newly added tests (e.g., GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testManageAllGroups: “fallback to all-groups permission”), so it is not a defect “silently” introduced but intended behavior. The claim that this makes group-level deny impossible and “order-dependent” cannot be verified from the diff (no deny semantics or ordering behavior is shown here).
